newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Well Rich signs US$115 mln Guangzhou project loan.
newsitem.headline: Well Rich signs US$115 mln Guangzhou project loan.

text.p: Well Rich Development Ltd's US$115 million non-recourse project term loan facility has been signed, lead arranger Sakura Bank said Thursday.
The borrower is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Cathay International Investment Co. Ltd.
Cathay International Investment Co.Ltd (CII) specialises in acquisition and development of infrastructure assets in China.

Through the borrower, CII holds a 60 percent stake in the Zhujiang Road Bridges and Tunnels Co Ltd. The remaining 40 percent is controlled by the Guangzhou Tunnels Development Co, an entity wholly-owned by the Guangzhou Municipal Government.
Proceeds are to be used for financing existing bridges and tunnel projects in Guangzhou.
The facility has a final maturity of seven years with no put or call options.
It pays a margin of 190 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return for participants is around 200 basis points.
The facility was around 20 percent oversubscribed and was scaled down at all levels, Sakura Bank noted.
Lead arrangers, with US$8.5 million each, are Banco Santander S.A., J.P Morgan Securities Asia, KEB Asia Finance, Sakura Bank, ST Capital, Union Bank of Switzerland.
Arrangers, with US$8.5 million each, are Credit Lyonnais, Korea Long Term Credit Bank and WestLB.
Co-arranger Mitsui Leasing and Development (Hong Kong) committed US$6 million.
Lead managers, with US$4 million each, are Bank of East Asia, KMBC Asia, Kyongnam Bank, Long Term Credit Bank of Japan, and Nippon Credit Bank Hong Kong.
Senior Managers, with US$2.5 million each, are Asiana (HK) Finance, DongNam Finance (Hong Kong), KDLC Lease and Finance, Saehan Asia Finance and United Chinese Bank.
